hypotheses.justification: Recover this from _hn because the real cast of Fintype.card I is nonnegative, including when I is empty. The existing proof then applies unchanged.
The injection i ↦ (none, i), together with Fintype.card_le_of_injective, gives card I ≤ card (Option K × I). Cast this inequality to ℝ and compose with _hd. This also works when I or K is empty.

In both applications of exists_affine_coefficient_haar_approximation, use max C 0 as the frequency bound. The original frequency bounds remain valid, and max C 0 ≤ Real.exp P follows from _hCP and Real.exp_pos. The conclusion is independent of C. This also handles empty frequency-indexing types.
The sum of the nonnegative norms ‖c false a‖ is nonnegative and is at most B by _hcoefficients false. Thus _hB follows, including when F is empty and the sum is zero.

Use max S 0 as the stride bound in both calls to exists_affine_coefficient_haar_approximation. The stride inequalities remain valid, and its exponential upper bound follows from _hSP and Real.exp_pos. S does not occur in the conclusion. This argument also handles empty I, where nonnegativity of the original S need not follow.

_hDmass makes the integral of D nonzero. Mathlib's MeasureTheory.Integrable.of_integral_ne_zero therefore recovers _hD. In particular, nonintegrable junk values cannot be a counterexample: integral_undef would make the integral zero, contradicting _hDmass.

Evaluate _happrox at b = false and x = 0. Its left side is a nonnegative complex norm, so η is nonnegative. CoefficientTorus is an additive-group quotient and always has zero, including in all empty or trivial indexing cases.
